blocking.problem: The closed-window exception does not reconcile the remaining source rules with its proposed realisation. §6.2 still requires each cleanup’s external input versions to be current. §11/K81 forms source pairs using §§5.3 and 6.2 before selecting realisations, and §11 retains source dependency ordering. The new text permits closed windows but neither identifies a legal earlier source cleanup as the reference nor expressly permits its relocation across those dependencies. This problem exists even without the optional clean-isometry extension: d=qcopy a; h a; quncopy a d cannot form the required source pair after H changes a. Its literal late inverse also supplies the wrong reference: on initial a=d=0 it produces (|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2), so d is one with probability 1/2. The desired measurement-assisted realisation instead produces |+>_a|0>_d. The exact helpers in docs/notes/2026-11-02-contract-verification.md reproduce these states as flip(hadamard(flip({0:ONE},1,(0,)),0),1,(0,)) and hadamard(flip(flip({0:ONE},1,(0,)),1,(0,)),0), respectively. The mechanism needs to decide which source operation is being implemented and how its delayed cleanup remains selectable.
blocking.fix: In §§6.2 and 11 add: “A measure_fixup witness binds a well-formed source computing/cleanup pair at its original K65 carrier and an explicit later realised cleanup location. Source pairing uses the original legal source versions. The witness MAY delay that cleanup across identified intervening operations, extending workspace lifetimes and replacing the corresponding scheduling dependency edges. The checker verifies the complete realised region channel against the unchanged well-formed source region, including all interface wires, inherited controls, borrowed systems and clean workspace restoration. The current-version and window restrictions remain mandatory for reverse/recompute; the checked relocation rule governs measure_fixup.” Give this corrected example: reference source d=qcopy a; quncopy a d; h a; realised sequence d=qcopy a; h a; X-measure d; apply H_a Z_a^m H_a=X_a^m; reset/release d. Each branch operator on a is H/sqrt(2), and input zero finishes as |+>_a with d clean. For the AND example, use reference C; cx g y; C†; release g; h a, whose interface operation is H_a CCX(a,b;y); the delayed realisation uses H_a CZ(a,b)^m H_a. Alternatively, introduce an explicit transported logical-cleanup source operation with a defined unitary reference and amend source pairing and grammar accordingly. I would take the legal-source/checked-relocation approach because it preserves existing source bytes and hashes.

blocking.problem: The diff adds channel claims and certificate cleanup witnesses but never states their use in a mixed fat object containing native host code and only marked device modules. Hiding private outcomes from the launch measurement list does not establish certificate inventory or subject scope. The binding standing check explicitly requires this statement for certificate-layout changes; its absence requires revise.
blocking.fix: In §§12.1–12.3 add: “A mixed fat object may contain native host code and multiple embedded ISA modules. Each channel subject identifies a region closure within its embedded device object and covers that region’s declared device interface and device callee closure. Native host entry points, argv/envp and unlifted native library code are outside that quantum channel subject. The default certificate layout is one certificate per embedded ISA object, with a fat-object inventory mapping each device module to its object_hash and certificate. Native comparison, where claimed, concerns the materialised outlined region and its materialised callee closure. Private cleanup outcomes remain internal to the device invocation and do not enter the host-visible measurement inventory.” A unified certificate with explicit per-module bindings is also viable; I would take the per-module default because it preserves the existing single-object bindings.
